method: Converts each port power from dBm to milliwatts with P = 10^(dBm/10) and works from the four measured powers P1 (input), P2 (through), P3 (coupled) and P4 (isolated). Coupling is C = 10 log10(P1/P3), directivity is D = 10 log10(P3/P4), isolation is I = 10 log10(P1/P4), which equals C + D, and insertion loss is IL = 10 log10(P1/P2). The coupled and through fractions are P3/P1 and P2/P1, and the four-port power total is (P2 + P3 + P4)/P1, which a passive coupler cannot push above 100 percent; a total above 101 percent raises a measurement warning. Directivity assumes the through port is terminated in a matched load, so P4 is leakage through the coupler rather than a reflection from the load. Each power must be a number from -100 to 100 dBm; the coupled power must be below the input, the isolated power may not exceed the coupled power, and the through power may not exceed the input. Warnings are shown for directivity below 10 dB (or essentially zero), coupling above 30 dB, insertion loss above 1 dB and an impossible power total. Results are rounded to two decimals for the dB values and percentages, except the through fraction and the power total, which use one decimal. Power-meter accuracy, mismatch uncertainty, coupler loss and the effect of a reflective load are not modelled, and everything runs in the browser with no storage or network access.
